**Answer.** Yes, and the second view corrects the first. Both store photographs are taken from ABOVE — the fits return [20°]{.key} and [36°]{.key} of elevation — so the [initial reconstruction](2026-10-07-01-can-we-reconstruct-the-ft-f-16-viper-within-tolerance.qmd) was never checked against an underside at all, and this entry originally said otherwise because the reference photograph was labelled and described as a belly view when it is not. What the second frame adds is a second azimuth, not a second hemisphere: the bubble canopy, dorsal spine, leading-edge strakes and wingtip rails are seen twice from different bearings, and the fuselage underside and ventral fin remain unverified by any photograph (@fig-overlays).

The studio pose sits at azimuth [210°]{.key} and roll [\-12\.8°]{.key}, for an outline residual of [2\.03%]{.key} of mask scale. The in-flight frame sits at azimuth [119°]{.key} and returns [2\.90%]{.key}. Both poses are good and neither is improved by a second seed, so what is left is the model's shape rather than the camera's — unmodelled wingtip ordnance, canopy frame thickness and intake ducting. No gross loft or planform error is hidden in either bearing.
